About the data

How the analysis works

The serve is shot one. The main chart can include the missed attempt. The point log always reports shots put in play. Aces and double faults have separate categories.

In Match view, each measured winner or unforced error counts once. Across matches, we average within each game first. A game contributes to an ending’s average only if it contains that ending. Service games, return games and tiebreaks each count once.

We check who hit the last shot, remove duplicate points and set aside matches with conflicting point records or unclear game numbers.

Limitations

Volunteers choose which matches to chart, and some records end early. A verified final score confirms the match result. The point log may still be incomplete.

Chartists judge whether a miss was forced. Points with unclear endings count toward game totals. Only known endings with a recorded length contribute to rally averages.

Surface, opponent and server can all affect the results. Winning more long rallies in one match doesn’t establish that prolonging a rally helps a player win.

Definitions
Winner
A shot that wins the point outright, such as a forehand down the line that passes the opponent untouched. We count aces separately.
Forced and unforced errors
On a forced error, the chartist judges that the opponent’s shot caused the miss. On an unforced error, the player misses a ball the chartist considers playable.
Last shot attempted
The shot number on which the point ended. A miss on shot five counts as the fifth attempt.
Shots in play
Count the legal serve as shot one. A winner on shot five counts as five shots in play. A miss on the same attempt leaves four.
Endings per game
Divide the player’s endings of one kind by all charted games, including service games, return games and tiebreaks.
Game-average share
Find the percentage of points in each game that ended with the player’s winner or, for the error statistic, their unforced error. Average those percentages.
Sources and code

Jeff Sackmann and the volunteers at Tennis Abstract’s Match Charting Project compiled the men’s and women’s point records. See the coverage notes for the match chartist’s name when available.

Source data for this version · Data license (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

Match scores come from Jeff Sackmann’s ATP and WTA singles results in the pinned results archive. Scores appear for unique matches on names, tour, tournament, surface, round and date window.
